Subject: Q2 pipeline taxonomy reset + micro-training (mandatory for AEs)

Team —

Quick heads-up: after a review with Finance and GTM Ops we are updating the way we classify deals in the forecast. The goal is to reduce ambiguous stage tagging and make commit signals consistent across regions so our month-end reconciles are predictable. This affects Commit / Best Case / Pipeline definitions and the tagging rules in Salesforce.

What changed (summary):
- Commit = active verbal agreement + legal intake started OR contract uploaded to SF (probability: 85%+)
- Best Case = sales-led confidence + committed next-step within 14 days (probability: 50–70%)
- Pipeline = all active opportunities that have been touched in last 60 days (probability: 10–40%)

Why this matters:
- Finance needs clearer thresholds to reconcile ACV/ARR month-to-month.
- Ops wants cleaner stage transitions to power rollup dashboards and automation (quota credit, bookings forecasts).

Attachments: Q2_forecast_taxonomy_v1.pdf (definitions + tagging map), example-deal-tagging.csv (sample SF records).

Immediate asks (please act by EOD Friday):
1) Update stage tags on all open Opps you own to match the new taxonomy (use the tagging map attached).
2) Ensure any opportunity you plan to mark as Commit has either a contract in SF OR an intake ticket created with Legal.
3) RSVP for a 30-minute micro-training (mandatory for AEs; SMs optional but encouraged) — calendar link below.

Micro-training: 30 mins, focused examples + Q&A. We will record and publish the recording for folks who can’t attend. Sessions: Apr 11 10:00am PT (primary), Apr 12 5:00pm BST (EMEA).
https://calendar.redwood.com/event/7f4a2b2c-q2-taxonomy-microtraining

If you hit edge cases (enterprise deals, carve-outs), call them out in the spreadsheet column labeled "exceptions" so Ops can surface them to Finance.

Thanks — let’s get this tidy before the close window.

Priyom
Priyom Das | Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
